title: Semantics and meaning in the Age of AI: Connected Data London 2026 | James Hendler & Juan Sequeda
description:
25 years later, the Semantic Web is being reinvented and co-opted..and that's a good thing

They say imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

They also say timing is everything.

25 years ago, the Semantic Web gave the world a set of principles and standards that help add meaning and grounding to data.

For a long time, the world was more concerned about quantity than quality.

Meaning and semantics was overlooked while pipelines and big data were top of mind.

Knowledge Graphs and Ontologies, while universally applicable, were reserved for a select few.

Today, the world is waking up to the importance of the principles and standards established by the Semantic Web.

The technology stack has matured and evolved significantly, with rising adoption driving a new wave of evolution.

While the journey has not been easy or flawless, the destination is in sight.

James Hendler is one of the authors of the original Semantic Web paper.

Juan Sequeda is one of the people who has spent the last 2 decades bringing the Semantic Web principles, standards and technology to life in the real world.

In this welcome address of the Connected Data London's 2026 Community Dinner, they put things into perspective, using both facts and a fun sketch.

It's funny because it's true.

All talk recordings from the event are being processed and will be available in the next few days.

With so many amazing ideas and speakers at #CDL26, nobody could possibly catch them all in real-time.

We've got you covered.
